title: An open access, machine learning pipeline for high-throughput quantification of cell morphology
protocol: Open the previously trained ilastik Pixel Classification file.
Set the desired export location for the resulting Prediction Maps.
Choose Prediction Export.
Select Choose Export Image Settings.
Select Directory.
Convert data to unsigned 16-bit format.
Renormalize from 0.00, 1.00 to 0, 65535.
Transpose axis order to cyx.
Set output file format to tif sequence.
Configure File Pattern as “nickname_result_type_slice_index.tif”.
Open a new Pixel Classification module.
Choose brightfield images that are representative of the dataset.
Input these representative images into the Input Data section.
Select sigma value features under Feature Selection.
Add three classes of labels under Training for the Cell Body, Background, and Boundary of the image.
Annotate a minimum of 25% of a single image with all three labels.
Add further annotations on additional images as necessary based on pipeline performance and variability.
Set location for exporting results under Prediction Export.
If previous training needs to be changed, add or remove annotations under Training in any of the three label classes.
Review the uncertainty filter if results are not satisfactory.
Make annotations in regions with high uncertainty.
Import experimental data including images into Batch Processing.
Select Process all files to allow the program to run.
Export three versions of each input image to the chosen location.
Use Probability Map Zero for the following steps.
Import the DAPI image and probability map of the first field into ImageJ/Fiji.
Convert both images into 8-bit format (Image > Type > 8-bit).
Threshold the DAPI image (Image > Adjust > Threshold) on the B&W default setting so that all nuclei are in black and the background is in white.
Use the Watershed function to separate overlapping nuclei.
Overlay the binary nuclei image with the probability map.
Set the DAPI image as the gray channel and the probability map as blue.
Convert the resulting image from 8-bit to RGB color.
Convert the image back to 8-bit, making it black and white.
Save this image for analysis.
Identify cell bodies and associate them with nuclei identified in the previous module.
Convert identified cell bodies to an image for subsequent processing.
Drag all files for one experimental group into the images section.
Check the quality of the image analysis.
Click the green Start Test Mode button at the bottom of the screen.
Step through the modules using the Step button for each image.
Move to the next image by clicking the Next Image Set button.
Check the IdentifySecondaryObjects module carefully.
Compare the colorful identification of cells to the original brightfield image.
Ensure that the shapes of cells in the brightfield image are accurately depicted in the identification image.
Note which images are of acceptable quality.
After ensuring results from the IdentifySecondaryObjects module are satisfactory, check the IdentifyPrimaryObjects and MorphologicalSkeleton modules.
Exit test mode.
Remove unsatisfactory images for analysis.
Edit the ExporttoSpreadsheet module to reflect the desired save location.
Quantify images using the Analyze Images button.
Repeat steps 7b–10 for any remaining experimental groups.
Keep a record of accepted and rejected images at various stages.
Document reasons for image rejection in an excel file with columns for each stage.
